rationale.conceptual: The paper's own custom multi-physics model requires genuine understanding of Biot poroelasticity, Onsager's law, and FEM discretization. Implementing the coupled equations (stiffness, Poisson's, volumetric strain evolution, 1D ionic transport) with weak coupling involves non-trivial math translation and careful numerical programming, going well beyond textbook or library-call tasks.
rationale.execution: A multi-stage pipeline: build the FE solver (a heavy process step), run passive simulation, run active simulation with intermediate HDF5 file, and extract two scored outputs. The orchestration is moderate (~4-5 steps) but straightforward, relying on standard Python/NumPy/SciPy without tricky tooling, so execution complexity is in the 3-4 range, leaning higher due to the solver construction being the main load.

The solver must be coded and used to simulate passive stress relaxation and active cation insertion. The pipeline involves several stages (build solver, run two simulations, extract results) but relies on standard Python libraries and no complex orchestration. The computational scale is modest (small mesh, no external data), only CPU needed.
